resources.name: SWE-Gym
resources.size: 2,438 train instances from 11 Python repos (HF split count)
resources.summary: Real GitHub issue tasks with FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests, built for training and verifying SWE agents. Lite (230) and Raw (64,689 unvalidated PR rows) variants exist.
resources.how_to_use: Use as a small, clean RL pool with per-repo Docker images from the SWE-Gym repo; pair with the SWE-bench test harness as verifier. Combine with larger sets for scale.
resources.caveats: Small. Only 2.4k tasks, so pass-rate filtering leaves little. Repo overlap with SWE-bench test repos is a known contamination concern for SWE-bench evals. Images must be built or pulled separately.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-Gym/SWE-Gym", split="train")

resources.name: SWE-smith
resources.summary: Synthetic bug-injection tasks generated per repo (LM-written, rewritten, procedural and PR-mirror bugs) with test-based validation and per-task Docker image names. Java and other-language variants are listed under SWE-bench on HF.
resources.how_to_use: Large cheap source of verifiable SWE tasks. Filter by pass rate of your current policy before RL; use the image_name column to pull per-task containers.
resources.caveats: Synthetic bugs are easier and less natural than real issues; problem statements are LM generated. Nemotron-Cascade used it as one of five sources, not alone. Check test-leak risk: FAIL_TO_PASS tests are present in the repo image.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench/SWE-smith", split="train")

resources.name: SWE-rebench (nebius, v1)
resources.summary: Continuously mined Python GitHub issue tasks with install configs, F2P/P2P tests and docker_image names, from Nebius; also feeds a decontaminated leaderboard.
resources.how_to_use: Use the filtered split for quality; docker_image/install_config let you reproduce environments. Good RL pool next to SWE-Gym and R2E-Gym.
resources.caveats: The huge test split is unfiltered: some tasks have ambiguous statements or weak tests. Underlying repo licenses vary (license_name column). Check time overlap with your eval set.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-rebench", split="filtered")

resources.name: SWE-rebench V2
resources.summary: Language-agnostic executable SWE tasks with pre-built images, F2P/P2P tests and LLM quality filtering. A companion set has 126,300 PR-derived tasks.
resources.how_to_use: Best open multilingual SWE RL pool as of late 2026. Start with the issue-linked set, add the PRs set for volume after filtering.
resources.caveats: PR-derived tasks lack issue text quality guarantees. Images are large. Repo licenses vary (license column). Leaderboard maintained for V1 Python only per HF discussion.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-rebench-V2", split="train")

resources.name: R2E-Gym (Subset)
resources.summary: Procedurally generated executable environments from commits (back-translated issue text, LM-generated tests) used to train SWE agents and verifiers; includes dev splits in the Lite variant.
resources.how_to_use: Use as a second RL source beside real-issue sets; pull images named in docker_image.
resources.caveats: Problem statements are back-translated, tests partly LM-written, so label noise exists. Code repo last pushed 2025-07-13. The Lite variant card has no license field.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("R2E-Gym/R2E-Gym-Subset", split="train")

resources.name: SWE-bench-extra
resources.summary: Nebius earlier large SWE-bench-format task collection (patch, test_patch, F2P/P2P, license per instance), precursor to SWE-rebench.
resources.how_to_use: Mostly superseded by SWE-rebench; still usable for SFT or RL if you build the environments yourself.
resources.caveats: No image columns, so environments must be reconstructed. Superseded by SWE-rebench.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nebius/SWE-bench-extra", split="train")

resources.name: SWE-bench (full, train/test splits)
resources.license: MIT (GitHub repo; HF card has no license field)
resources.size: 2,294 test + 225 dev instances in the HF repo; no train split listed
resources.summary: The original 2,294-issue benchmark, now with eval_script, image and log_parser columns. A SWE-bench-Train subset (1,063 questions per the Nemotron-Cascade card) was used by Nemotron-Cascade.
resources.how_to_use: Treat as eval, not training. If using the old train data, exclude repos in your eval set as Nemotron-Cascade did.
resources.caveats: The HF repo currently exposes test/dev only (verified 2026-11-24). Train data cited by Nemotron-Cascade came from princeton-nlp/SWE-bench; repo overlap contaminates Verified/Lite evals. Git history leak was patched upstream (PR 471).
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench/SWE-bench", split="test")

resources.name: SWE-bench-Live
resources.size: 1,000 test, 1,888 full, 300 lite, 500 verified instances (split counts)
resources.summary: Continuously updated issue-resolution benchmark with docker_image, test_cmds and rebuild_cmds per task, intended to stay ahead of contamination.
resources.how_to_use: Use older monthly slices as extra RL data only if you keep recent months held out.
resources.caveats: Designed as eval; training on it burns the contamination guarantee. Split definitions may change between updates.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("SWE-bench-Live/SWE-bench-Live", split="full")

resources.name: Multi-SWE-RL
resources.size: Community RL dataset, first batch data_20240601_20250331; per-language counts not machine-readable on the card
resources.summary: ByteDance Seed community effort to collect multilingual SWE RL instances (unannotated new instances plus discarded Multi-SWE-bench instances).
resources.how_to_use: Treat as raw material: you must build environments with the multi-swe-bench toolkit before using it for RL.
resources.caveats: Unannotated and license is vague ('other'). Last HF update 2025-07-23. Little documentation of sizes in the card, so size is not verified.

resources.name: SWE-Dev
resources.summary: Feature-driven development tasks: product requirement, partial source, developer-written unit tests and ground-truth code, supporting SFT and RL with test-based reward.
resources.how_to_use: Use for feature implementation (not bug fixing) RL, executing the bundled unit tests as reward.
resources.caveats: Exact train/test counts not verified here. A separate zai-org/SWE-Dev-train holds SFT/RFT trajectories (17,871 sft, 2,276 rft rows) with no license on its card. GitHub code repo has no license.

resources.name: SWE-Synth
resources.license: none stated on dataset card (null in API)
resources.summary: Synthetic bug-fix instances with setup patches, F2P/P2P tests and problem statements, plus Moatless SFT trajectories in sibling datasets.
resources.how_to_use: Use as additional synthetic SWE data after checking license with authors.
resources.caveats: No license on card, so redistribution rights unclear. Last updated 2025-03.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("swesynth/SWE-Synth", split="train")

resources.name: SWE-Flow / Repo2RLEnv swe_flow recipe
resources.size: SWE-Flow code; Repo2RLEnv sample set FineEnvs/repo2rlenv-swe-flow has 100 Harbor tasks
resources.summary: Test-driven synthesis: trace passing tests, remove exercised functions, ask the agent to reconstruct them, reward via retained tests. Hugging Face Repo2RLEnv now packages the recipe as Harbor tasks.
resources.how_to_use: Use Repo2RLEnv to turn your own repos into Harbor-format RL tasks.
resources.caveats: Sample HF set is only 100 tasks with mixed source licenses. SWE-Flow repo last pushed 2025-06-29 with 40 stars.

resources.name: Repo2RLEnv
resources.summary: Hugging Face tool that turns any repository into verifiable RL environments for coding agents in Harbor task format (instruction, Dockerfile, tests, reward script).
resources.how_to_use: Use to build private RL tasks from your own codebases with the same format as Terminal-Bench 2.
resources.caveats: Young project; recipe quality varies. Verify tests cannot be edited by the agent in each generated task.

resources.name: OpenSWE (GAIR, daVinci-Env)
resources.license: other (gated, access conditions on card); code repo licensed per GitHub as NOASSERTION; search snippet says AGPL-3.0 (unverified)
resources.size: 10K-100K rows (HF size category); paper claims 45,320 Docker environments
resources.summary: Large open set of executable Python SWE environments with synthesis pipeline released.
resources.how_to_use: Request access, read license terms, then use for large-scale RL after pass-rate filtering.
resources.caveats: Gated with auto-approval; license ambiguous. Counts from paper abstract via search, not confirmed from API.

resources.name: Lego-RL-2699 and LegoFlow-SWE
resources.size: 1K-10K Harbor RL environments (HF size category); Verified-500 packaged as Harbor tasks
resources.summary: SWE-Lego family: Harbor-format RL environments, teacher trajectories and a Harbor-packaged SWE-bench Verified for evaluating against the same trainer.
resources.how_to_use: Use if your trainer reads Harbor tasks; check AGPL implications before redistributing derived data.
resources.caveats: AGPL-3.0 on RL set is restrictive. LEGO-RL paper id seen in card (2608.17393) not independently opened. SWE-Lego code repo Apache-2.0.

resources.name: Nemotron-Cascade-RL-SWE
resources.size: Per card (16K-prompt slice): 23,236 SWE-Fixer, 2,472 SWE-Smith (card prints '24,72'), 1,063 SWE-Bench-Train, 4,244 SWE-rebench questions
resources.summary: NVIDIA recipe data for SWE RL: difficulty-filtered mix of SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-rebench, SWE-smith, R2E-Gym-Subset and SWE-Fixer, with repos from SWE-bench Verified excluded to avoid contamination.
resources.how_to_use: Take as a template for mixing five sources and excluding eval repos. Reward there is execution-free (reward model), not Docker.
resources.caveats: Card states no Docker execution reward was used, so this is not an execution-verified recipe. Question counts are on the card; the SWE-Smith figure is garbled on the card.

resources.name: NVIDIA SWE-Zero / SWE-Hero OpenHands trajectories
resources.summary: OpenHands agent trajectories with model_patch and repo license columns, for SFT or rejection sampling on SWE tasks.
resources.how_to_use: Filter by resolved status and license column before SFT.
resources.caveats: Resolve labels are not in the verified column list (instance_id, repo, license, trajectory_id, trajectory, model_patch, dataset). Teacher-model terms apply; check card.

resources.name: DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset
resources.size: 24K problems with tests per card; configs lcbv5 (599 train, 279 test) and codeforces (408 test) verified in API
resources.summary: Verified-test competitive programming set used to train DeepCoder-14B: TACO verified, PrimeIntellect SYNTHETIC-1 code and LiveCodeBench problems with test lists.
resources.how_to_use: Standard small RL pool for GRPO code runs; run tests with a sandbox (SandboxFusion, verl's code reward).
resources.caveats: Includes LiveCodeBench v5 train problems, so do not eval on lcbv5 train/test overlap. Only 2 of the configs inspected; 24K figure from card.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("agentica-org/DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset", "lcbv5", split="train")

resources.name: open-r1/codeforces
resources.size: 10,024 problems (9,556 train + 468 test); verifiable config 8,338 train + 422 test
resources.summary: Codeforces problems with statements, editorials, official tests and generated checkers, including interactive problems; the 'verifiable' config keeps problems with complete tests.
resources.how_to_use: Use the verifiable config for RL; run C++/Python with checker support. Problems carry a rating column for difficulty filtering.
resources.caveats: Needs a judge that handles special checkers and interactors. Statements are scraped from codeforces.com (card gives CC-BY-4.0; rights to original content not verified).
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("open-r1/codeforces", "verifiable", split="train")

resources.name: CodeContests (DeepMind)
resources.summary: Competitive problems from Codeforces, CodeChef, AtCoder and others with generated tests and correct/incorrect human solutions in Python, C++ and Java.
resources.how_to_use: Classic source of RL problems; many prepared versions exist (Eurus-2, Nemotron-RL).
resources.caveats: False-positive rate of original generated tests is high; CodeContests+ and CodeContests-O exist to fix this. Python 2 solutions present.

resources.name: TACO
resources.summary: Large algorithmic problem set with tests, solutions, difficulty and algorithm tags, aggregated from many contest sites.
resources.how_to_use: Use difficulty/skill tags for curriculum; filter via the verified subset in DeepCoder-Preview-Dataset.
resources.caveats: Raw test quality varies (DeepCoder filtered to a verified subset). Upstream site terms not fully clear.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("BAAI/TACO", "ALL", split="train")

resources.name: APPS
resources.summary: Interview-level and competition Python problems with solutions and test cases.
resources.how_to_use: Old but common RL sanity set; heavily contaminated in modern pretraining data.
resources.caveats: Known noisy tests and duplicates. Prefer cleaned derivatives.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("codeparrot/apps", split="train")

resources.name: CodeContests+
resources.summary: CodeContests with LLM-generated, validated test generators and checkers to raise test quality, built using SandboxFusion; intended as better RL verifiers.
resources.how_to_use: Prefer over raw CodeContests for RL reward accuracy.
resources.caveats: Larger test multiplicities cost more sandbox time. Sandbox required.

resources.name: CodeContests-O
resources.license: not stated in card header (API license null); check card
resources.size: 11,407 train + 162 test + 114 valid problems; dataset_size about 714 GB
resources.summary: Feedback-driven iterative test case generation for CodeContests problems: generators, checkers and corner cases.
resources.how_to_use: Use the generators rather than download the whole set; partial download by file.
resources.caveats: Enormous (about 325 GB download). License unspecified. Paper arXiv 2601.13682.

resources.name: Skywork-OR1-RL-Data
resources.license: Apache-2.0 on GitHub repo; HF card has no license field
resources.summary: RL-ready math and code problems in verl format (prompt, reward_model.ground_truth) with per-model pass difficulty labels for 1.5B, 7B and 32B R1 distills.
resources.how_to_use: Use extra_info.model_difficulty to drop always-solved and never-solved items before GRPO.
resources.caveats: Card license missing. Code ground truth are large test blobs (about 1.5 GB for 14k code rows).
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("Skywork/Skywork-OR1-RL-Data", split="code")

resources.name: SYNTHETIC-1
resources.size: 1,994,262 rows; card sections: 777k math, 144k algorithmic coding, 70k SWE, 61k code understanding
resources.summary: Prime Intellect crowdsourced DeepSeek-R1 traces with verification_info and score columns across math, coding, SWE and more.
resources.how_to_use: Filter by score and task_type for verified-correct traces or reuse problems with verification_info for RL.
resources.caveats: R1-generated; check DeepSeek license terms. Wide mix, many non-code rows.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("PrimeIntellect/SYNTHETIC-1", split="train")

resources.name: Eurus-2-RL-Data
resources.summary: PRIME RL training set: outcome-verifiable math answers and coding test cases from APPS, CodeContests, TACO and Codeforces, deduplicated.
resources.how_to_use: Early baseline mix for outcome-reward RL.
resources.caveats: Cleaning was mostly deduplication, so test quality is raw.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("PRIME-RL/Eurus-2-RL-Data", split="train")

resources.name: Nemotron-RL-coding-competitive_coding
resources.license: CC-BY-SA-4.0 in card metadata, card text says CC-BY-4.0 (inconsistent)
resources.size: 16,083 train rows in metadata; card text says 25k records, 7.62 GB
resources.summary: NeMo Gym RLVR set of Python competitive problems with unit tests from CodeContests and open-r1/codeforces.
resources.how_to_use: Use with NeMo Gym or convert to verl format.
resources.caveats: License inconsistency and count mismatch between YAML and prose; confirm before redistribution. Tests are inlined, so about 5 GB.

resources.name: KodCode-V1
resources.summary: Fully synthetic coding questions with solutions and pytest-style tests validated by execution; fields include gpt pass percentage and difficulty.
resources.how_to_use: Use gpt_pass_percentage and gpt_difficulty to select medium difficulty for RL; tests are runnable.
resources.caveats: Non-commercial license. Generated with GPT-4 family so OpenAI terms may apply. Easier than competition sets.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("KodCode/KodCode-V1", split="train")

resources.name: rStar-Coder
resources.summary: Competitive problems with mutually verified test cases, with configs synthetic_sft, synthetic_rl, synthetic_rl_testcase, seed_sft, seed_testcase.
resources.how_to_use: Use synthetic_rl plus synthetic_rl_testcase for RL; seed_* configs have real problems.
resources.caveats: Test cases live in separate config, join by id. Large. Solutions from Qwen/DeepSeek models.

resources.name: OpenCodeReasoning
resources.summary: R1-generated reasoning solutions for competitive problems with difficulty column and source license column.
resources.how_to_use: Use for SFT warm start before RL; join split_1 to original problems by index.
resources.caveats: split_1 lacks question text and needs reconstruction from source datasets.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nvidia/OpenCodeReasoning", "split_0", split="split_0")

resources.name: LiveCodeBench
resources.size: 980 stars; problem releases dated by contest
resources.summary: Contamination-aware benchmark from LeetCode, AtCoder and Codeforces with problem release dates; DeepCoder used the lcbv5 train problems for RL.
resources.how_to_use: Use date filtering to keep eval clean of your RL data.
resources.caveats: Repo last pushed 2025-07-16. Training on recent problems makes it unusable as eval.

resources.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
resources.size: under 1K tasks (HF size category); read-only mirror
resources.summary: Hard terminal tasks in Harbor format (instruction, Docker environment, tests); official leaderboard at tbench.ai. Also terminal-bench 2.1, 3.0 and a science split on HF.
resources.how_to_use: Run with Harbor; use as eval, and use Harbor task format to author RL tasks.
resources.caveats: Few tasks so not an RL pool; HF page is a mirror, primary repo is GitHub. Unofficial leaderboard warning on card.

resources.name: Spider
resources.summary: Cross-domain text-to-SQL; databases are executable SQLite so execution accuracy gives a reward.
resources.how_to_use: Train GRPO with execution-match reward on SQLite, compare result sets.
resources.caveats: Saturated for strong models; the HF dataset has questions and gold SQL but SQLite databases come from the Spider site or a separate dataset.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("xlangai/spider", "spider", split="train")

resources.name: BIRD mini-dev and BIRD-Critic
resources.size: bird_mini_dev (1K-10K rows by size category); BIRD-Critic SQLite also on HF
resources.summary: Harder, more realistic text-to-SQL with execution-based evaluation; BIRD-Critic covers SQL debugging with test cases.
resources.how_to_use: Use BIRD train (birdsql/bird23-train-filtered) for execution-reward RL; mini-dev for eval.
resources.caveats: Exact row counts not read here. BIRD train is older and sometimes noisy. Execution match can be gamed by empty or equivalent result sets.

resources.name: Lean Workbook
resources.summary: Auto-formalized competition-style problems in Lean 4, used for theorem-prover RL; Goedel-LM/Lean-workbook-proofs has 29,750 proofs.
resources.how_to_use: Verifier is the Lean 4 compiler (kimina-lean-server, Lean REPL); filter by pass rate.
resources.caveats: Auto-formalization noise: some statements trivial or false. Compiler checks proof validity only, not statement faithfulness.

resources.summary: Lean benchmark for end-to-end verified code generation: specification and implementation proven correct.
resources.how_to_use: Use as eval or hard RL seed.

resources.name: HumanEval
resources.summary: Function-from-docstring Python problems with unit tests, introduced with Codex. The original functional-correctness benchmark.
resources.how_to_use: Use only as a cheap smoke test that a code model is not broken. Do not use it to rank current models. Runs in seconds to minutes on one GPU.
resources.caveats: Execution-based (unit tests). Saturated: current frontier models are near ceiling, so differences are mostly noise. Public since 2021 and widely copied, so contamination is likely in web-scale pretraining data; the EvalPlus paper also showed the original tests are too weak (see HumanEval+). Measures short self-contained function synthesis only; not repo context, debugging, or design. Historical score in the paper abstract: Codex 28.8% (arXiv 2107.03374).

resources.caveats: Mostly exact-match and edit-similarity, not execution-based. Built from public GitHub code, so contamination is likely for models trained on it.

resources.name: CrossCodeEval
resources.size: multi-language cross-file completion set (count not extracted)
resources.summary: Completion tasks that cannot be solved without cross-file context, in several languages, with static-analysis-based construction.
resources.how_to_use: Use to test retrieval-augmented completion; pair with RepoBench.
resources.caveats: Match-based metrics, not execution-based. Built from open-source repos so leakage possible. Task count and language list not extracted in this pass.

resources.name: SAFIM (Syntax-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle)
resources.summary: FIM benchmark focused on syntactic structures (blocks, conditionals, API calls), with problems sourced after April 2022 to reduce contamination.
resources.how_to_use: Use to evaluate FIM ability of base and code-completion models; mix of execution-based and syntactic matching depending on subtask.
resources.caveats: Per the paper, execution-based tests for algorithmic subsets; the contamination window is limited to data after April 2022 so newer models may have seen it.

resources.name: CanItEdit
resources.summary: Hand-crafted instructional code editing problems with descriptive and lazy instruction variants, tested by execution.
resources.how_to_use: Cheap check of instruction-following edits; run when training on commit or edit data.
resources.caveats: Execution-based. Small (105). Python only; public since 2023-24. GitHub repo license field shows NOASSERTION; HF card says MIT.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset("nuprl/CanItEdit", split="test")

resources.name: DevEval (SDLC benchmark, arXiv 2403.08604)
resources.size: multi-stage tasks, four languages (counts not extracted)
resources.summary: Evaluates LLMs across the software lifecycle: design, environment setup, implementation, acceptance and unit testing. Note the name clashes with other 'DevEval'/'DevBench' projects.
resources.how_to_use: Reference only; low adoption. Check which 'DevBench' or 'DevEval' you mean before citing.
resources.caveats: Part LLM-judged, part test-based. I did not find a verified data release in this pass. Title is a case study, not a mature leaderboard.

resources.name: ProjectEval
resources.summary: Project-level generation benchmark with three input levels, evaluated by simulated user interaction plus code similarity.
resources.how_to_use: Niche; consider for web-app generation agents.
resources.caveats: Benchmark built by an LLM with human review; uses simulated user interaction for execution. I did not verify a repo or data link.

resources.name: Commit0
resources.summary: Agent must implement a library from its spec using interactive unit tests; measures long-form spec following.
resources.how_to_use: Use as an expensive stress test for from-scratch library generation.
resources.caveats: Execution-based (unit tests). Small (54 libraries). Repo last pushed 2026-02. Libraries are public so leakage is possible. HF dataset metadata has no license field.

resources.name: MLE-bench
resources.summary: Agents train models, prepare data and run experiments on real Kaggle competitions, graded against human leaderboards.
resources.how_to_use: Only relevant for ML-engineering agents; very expensive (GPU hours per task).
resources.caveats: Execution and leaderboard-based. Paper abstract: o1-preview with AIDE reached at least bronze in 16.9% of competitions (2024). Needs Kaggle data downloads and GPUs.

resources.name: PaperBench
resources.summary: Agents replicate ML papers from scratch; rubric-graded by an LLM judge. Also ported to inspect_evals (paperbench).
resources.how_to_use: Niche research-agent eval; very expensive.
resources.caveats: Not execution-only: scoring uses an LLM judge with author-co-developed rubrics. License of the official data not verified here.

resources.name: SWE-Lancer
resources.license: repo openai/SWELancer-Benchmark: no license field; archived
resources.size: 1,400+ freelance Upwork tasks worth $1M in payouts
resources.summary: Independent engineering tasks graded by end-to-end tests plus managerial decisions, mapped to real payouts.
resources.how_to_use: Optional; also available in inspect_evals (swe_lancer). Expensive.
resources.caveats: Execution-based for IC tasks (e2e tests triple-verified), proposal-matching for manager tasks. The original GitHub repo is archived as of 2026-11-24 and only a subset was public.

resources.name: METR time-horizon task suite (HCAST, RE-Bench)
resources.size: tasks from RE-Bench, HCAST and 66 shorter tasks (per paper)
resources.summary: Measures the 50% task-completion time horizon: the human task length models complete at 50% success. Reported to double about every seven months since 2019.
resources.how_to_use: Use as a long-horizon pointer for how agent capability scales with task duration; not a practical training gate.
resources.caveats: Per paper abstract, Claude 3.7 Sonnet had about a 50-minute horizon (early 2025). Not all tasks are public (the METR/public-tasks repo is archived). Time horizon depends on human baselines and task mix.

resources.name: CyberSecEval (Purple Llama)
resources.size: multi-suite; insecure code generation plus cyberattack compliance tests
resources.summary: Meta's suite for insecure-code generation and cyber misuse, with later versions adding more tests; also in inspect_evals (cyberseceval_2 to 4).
resources.how_to_use: Run as a safety gate for code models before release, alongside CWEval for dynamic checks.
resources.caveats: Original insecure-code tests use static analysis rules (CWEval's authors criticize unclear specs and impractical evaluation). Not execution-based for functionality. Repo license is mixed, so check it.

resources.name: SecCodePLT
resources.summary: Security benchmark built from validated seeds expanded by mutation, with dynamic tests for both code generation and cyberattack helpfulness.
resources.how_to_use: Add for secure-code evaluation with dynamic checks.
resources.caveats: Dynamic test-based. Gated (auto-approval). The paper (listed as SeCodePLT on arXiv) claims better coverage than static-rule benchmarks, which I did not independently check.

resources.name: CWEval
resources.summary: Outcome-driven evaluation of both functionality and security of generated code using test oracles for CWE-linked tasks.
resources.how_to_use: Cheap secure-code regression check next to HumanEval-style functional tests.
resources.caveats: Execution-based. Small, public since January 2025.

resources.name: TestGenEval
resources.size: 1,210 test split (code and test file pairs); 68,647 tests across 11 Python repos (paper)
resources.summary: Unit-test authoring and completion benchmark built from SWE-bench repositories, with a lite subset.
resources.how_to_use: Use when training test-writing ability; check coverage and mutation score outputs.
resources.caveats: Execution-based (coverage, mutation). Shares repos with SWE-bench, so overlap with SWE-bench-derived training data is likely. Splits seen: test 1,210, dev 210, train 15,439.

resources.name: SWT-Bench
resources.size: Verified variant 433 instances (HF eth-sri/SWT-bench_Verified_bm25_27k_zsb); also Lite
resources.summary: Agents write reproduction tests for real GitHub issues; a good test fails before and passes after the golden patch.
resources.how_to_use: Use to check whether agents can turn issues into fail-to-pass tests, a key skill for RL reward construction.
resources.caveats: Execution-based. Derived from SWE-bench so shares contamination concerns. HF license not stated.

resources.name: Defects4J
resources.size: database of real Java faults (count not extracted)
resources.summary: Classic real-fault Java repair and testing database with infrastructure; used by repair benchmarks such as RepairBench.
resources.how_to_use: Use for Java program repair evaluation; requires Java toolchains.
resources.caveats: Execution-based. Public since 2014, heavily contaminated in code training data; RepairBench (ASSERT-KTH/repairbench, no license field) is a leaderboard built on it.

resources.name: miniF2F
resources.summary: Formal Olympiad-level problems (AIME, AMC, IMO, coursework) in Lean and other systems for theorem proving.
resources.how_to_use: Use as the standard Lean theorem-proving gate; cheap relative to agentic evals.
resources.caveats: Verifier-checked (Lean). Heavily saturated by recent provers and public for years, so contamination is likely. The original openai/miniF2F repo is archived and has fixes elsewhere; use a corrected version.
resources.evidence: github.com/facebookresearch/miniF2F MIT; openai/miniF2F archived; arxiv.org/abs/2109.00110; HF HaimingW/miniF2F-lean4 splits

resources.name: PutnamBench
resources.license: no license field in GitHub metadata
resources.size: 1,692 formalizations of 640 Putnam theorems (Lean 4, Isabelle, partial Coq)
resources.summary: Hard undergraduate competition math formalizations for neural theorem provers.
resources.how_to_use: Use as the harder Lean gate beyond miniF2F. Expensive search-based proving.
resources.caveats: Verifier-checked. Maintained with an active leaderboard; repo pushed 2026-11-09. License field absent, so check the repo.

resources.name: EvalPlus CLI
resources.summary: Evaluation framework behind HumanEval+, MBPP+ and EvalPerf with backends for HF, vLLM, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Bedrock.
resources.how_to_use: Run evalplus.evaluate for correctness and evalplus.evalperf for efficiency; use evalplus.codegen to separate generation from sandboxed execution.
resources.caveats: Python-only function-level benchmarks. Last push 2025-10-02. Sandbox execution runs untrusted code, so use Docker.

resources.name: lm-evaluation-harness (code tasks)
resources.size: General LLM harness; code tasks include humaneval, humaneval_infilling, mbpp, code_x_glue
resources.summary: The standard few-shot LLM harness; code coverage is basic.
resources.how_to_use: Use for quick HumanEval/MBPP numbers inside a broader multi-task sweep; for serious code evaluation prefer EvalPlus or LiveCodeBench.
resources.caveats: Code tasks are thin; code execution requires explicit opt-in because it runs untrusted code.

resources.name: Inspect AI / inspect_evals
resources.size: Collection of community-maintained evals for Inspect AI
resources.summary: Large eval collection including apps, bigcodebench, class_eval, ds1000, humaneval, mbpp, usaco, swe_bench, swe_lancer, livecodebench_pro, mle_bench, paperbench and cyberseceval_2 to 4.
resources.how_to_use: Use when you want one sandboxed, agent-capable harness (Docker/K8s sandboxes) across coding and security evals; good for agentic gates.
resources.caveats: Third-party ports can differ in prompts and scoring from the original harness, so scores may not match published numbers. Actively maintained (pushed 2026-11-23).

resources.name: OpenCompass
resources.summary: Includes configs for bigcodebench, cruxeval, ds1000, humaneval (plus, multi, x, pro), livecodebench, livecodebench_pro and mbpp (plus, pro).
resources.how_to_use: Use for broad LLM leaderboards including code; large model-zoo support.
resources.caveats: Prompt formats may differ from original releases. Heavy configuration.

resources.name: lighteval
resources.summary: Evaluation library with LiveCodeBench tasks (src/lighteval/tasks/tasks/lcb) among many others.
resources.how_to_use: Use for HF-ecosystem evaluation with backends including vLLM; check task list for current code coverage.
resources.caveats: Code coverage smaller than dedicated harnesses; I saw LiveCodeBench only.
resources.evidence: github.com/huggingface/lighteval MIT pushed 2026-11-18; code search hit lcb

resources.name: EvalScope
resources.summary: Includes benchmarks for bigcodebench, ds1000, humaneval(plus), live_code_bench, mbpp(plus), swe_bench, swe_bench_pro and terminal_bench.
resources.how_to_use: Useful when you want one framework spanning generation and agentic coding benchmarks, plus performance stress testing.
resources.caveats: Many benchmark adapters; verify scoring against the original before comparing numbers.

resources.name: SWE-bench evaluation harness
resources.summary: Official Docker harness that applies model patches and runs repo tests, used by Verified, Lite, Multilingual and Multimodal.
resources.how_to_use: Run patches through it for any SWE-bench-format set; plan for large disk and many containers.
resources.caveats: Heavy on disk and CPU. Some downstream sets (SWE-bench-Live, Pro) ship their own harnesses.

resources.name: aider benchmark harness
resources.size: benchmark/ directory in the aider repo
resources.summary: Runs the polyglot benchmark in Docker against any model aider supports.
resources.how_to_use: Use to reproduce polyglot numbers for your own model endpoint.
resources.caveats: Last push 2026-05-22. Harness details are in aider docs; not re-verified here.

resources.name: Artificial Analysis (pointer)
resources.summary: Third-party site that aggregates model intelligence and coding indices; useful as a pointer to current coding scores.
resources.how_to_use: Check for an independent view across models; do not use as a training gate.
resources.caveats: Methodology and the set of benchmarks inside its coding index change; not verified in this pass.

resources.name: Magicoder OSS-Instruct 75K
resources.size: ~75K instruction-response pairs (per dataset name and paper)
resources.summary: Synthetic instructions generated by prompting an LLM with random open-source code snippets (OSS-Instruct) to reduce the bias of purely LLM-invented tasks.
resources.how_to_use: Good diverse seed for general code SFT; pair with Evol-style data (the paper reports the two are complementary). Check overlap before mixing with CodeFeedback, which re-uses it.
resources.caveats: Card states it was generated by gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 and warns to follow OpenAI's usage policy. No execution verification of solutions. Seeds come from public GitHub code.

resources.name: Magicoder Evol-Instruct 110K
resources.summary: Decontaminated version of theblackcat102/evol-codealpaca-v1 (WizardCoder-style Evol-Instruct on Code Alpaca seeds), decontaminated with the StarCoder/BigCode procedure.
resources.how_to_use: Use as the cleaner copy of the Evol-CodeAlpaca lineage. Combine with OSS-Instruct for a Magicoder-S style mix.
resources.caveats: Parent data was generated with gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 (per the evol-codealpaca-v1 card), so OpenAI terms apply. Decontamination covers older benchmarks only; recheck against newer evals.

resources.name: Evol-CodeAlpaca v1
resources.size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category); exact count not verified
resources.summary: Open re-creation of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data: Code Alpaca 20K evolved with 10 augmentation strategies and answered by GPT-4.
resources.how_to_use: Prefer the decontaminated Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K copy for training; use this one for lineage or research.
resources.caveats: Card says gpt-4-0314 and gpt-4-0613 produced the evolutions and answers (OpenAI terms apply). Not decontaminated against modern benchmarks in this original form.

resources.name: Evol-Instruct-Code-80k-v1
resources.summary: Community replication of the WizardCoder Evol-Instruct code data.
resources.how_to_use: Research use only because of the non-commercial license. Prefer evol-codealpaca-v1 or the Magicoder copy for commercial work.
resources.caveats: Non-commercial license. Generated with OpenAI models (not verified from the card; the card is minimal).

resources.name: Code Alpaca 20K
resources.summary: Self-Instruct-style code instruction set that started the open code-instruction line; seed of Evol-CodeAlpaca.
resources.how_to_use: Mostly historical. Small, noisy and easy; useful as a seed for evolution, not as a main SFT source.
resources.caveats: Project README says it was generated with Self-Instruct techniques and notes OpenAI TOS (text-davinci-003 per the Self-Instruct recipe; model name not confirmed on the card). Short, simple tasks; saturated.

resources.name: CodeFeedback-Filtered-Instruction
resources.summary: 287K queries from Magicoder-OSS, Python ShareGPT, Magicoder-Evol and Evol-Instruct, filtered to complexity 4-5 by Qwen-72B-Chat.
resources.how_to_use: Use when you want a complexity-filtered union of earlier instruction sets instead of the raw parents.
resources.caveats: Card warns that part of the data was generated by OpenAI models. Overlaps heavily with Magicoder data. Filter used a model-assigned complexity score, not execution.

resources.name: Code-Feedback (OpenCodeInterpreter)
resources.summary: Multi-turn code data with execution feedback and human-feedback-style follow-ups for iterative refinement (OpenCodeInterpreter).
resources.how_to_use: Include if you want a model that reads execution output and fixes its code over several turns.
resources.caveats: Card says part of it was generated by GPT-4-0613 and GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 (OpenAI usage policy applies). The headline 91.6 HumanEval/MBPP average in the paper used synthesized GPT-4 feedback at inference.

resources.name: StarCoder2 self-oss-instruct (SelfCodeAlign data)
resources.summary: Instruction data produced by StarCoder2-15B itself via the SelfCodeAlign pipeline (concept extraction, task generation, sampled responses with tests, execution filter). Used for StarCoder2-15B-Instruct.
resources.how_to_use: One of the few permissively usable SFT sets with no proprietary teacher; good default when you must avoid OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepSeek-derived outputs.
resources.caveats: Python only. The paper describes a transparent pipeline without distillation from a stronger model. Quality is bounded by the base model that generated it.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('bigcode/self-oss-instruct-sc2-exec-filter-50k', split='train')
# columns: instruction, response, prompt, seed, sha1, fingerprint, id

resources.name: CommitPackFT
resources.license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
resources.summary: Filtered subset of CommitPack where commit messages resemble natural-language instructions; basis of OctoPack/OctoCoder instruction tuning.
resources.how_to_use: Use for code-edit style instructions from real human commits with no LLM teacher. Per-language configs.
resources.caveats: Commit messages are noisy even after filtering. Predates modern evals. Contamination with benchmark repos should be checked.

resources.name: CommitPack
resources.license: MIT (HF card tag); per-file source licenses are permissive
resources.summary: Raw commit corpus (code before/after plus message) from which CommitPackFT was filtered.
resources.how_to_use: Use when you want to build your own commit-based edit data or commit-message models. Most SFT users want CommitPackFT instead.
resources.caveats: Very large and noisy. Not a download for low-resource machines.

resources.name: EditPackFT
resources.summary: Further-filtered CommitPackFT subset formatted for instructional code editing (before code, instruction, after code), used to train CanItEdit-evaluated models.
resources.how_to_use: Use to teach instruction-following code edits; evaluate with CanItEdit.
resources.caveats: Small. Derived from commit messages, so instruction quality varies.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nuprl/EditPackFT', split='train')
# columns include: instruction, old_contents, new_contents, lang, commit

resources.name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage1
resources.size: 3 configs: filtered_infinity_instruct, largescale_diverse_instruct, realuser_instruct; row counts not read
resources.summary: Stage-1 SFT mix of OpenCoder: filtered general instructions plus large-scale synthetic and real-user code instructions.
resources.how_to_use: Use as broad general-plus-code instruction data in a two-stage SFT recipe (general first, then code-heavy stage 2).
resources.caveats: Real-user part is extracted from ShareGPT/WildChat-style conversations, so it inherits their provenance and OpenAI-model responses (card says low-quality responses were regenerated; the generator model was not confirmed).

resources.name: OpenCoder opc-sft-stage2
resources.size: 4 configs: educational_instruct 118,278; evol_instruct 111,183; mceval_instruct 35,943; package_instruct 170,943 (dataset_info, split row counts)
resources.summary: High-quality stage-2 code SFT: educational synthetic, evolved, McEval-style multilingual and package-usage instructions.
resources.how_to_use: Use as the code-focused second SFT stage; the paper's recipe pairs it with stage 1.
resources.caveats: Teacher models per subset not confirmed from the card. Check for overlap with Evol-Instruct and Magicoder.

resources.name: Glaive Code Assistant v3
resources.summary: Synthetic code Q&A from Glaive's data platform; v3 includes v1 and v2.
resources.how_to_use: Cheap breadth for chat-style coding help; filter hard before using as a main source.
resources.caveats: Card does not name the generator model, so teacher provenance and terms are unknown. No execution verification stated.

resources.name: Ling-Coder-SFT
resources.summary: Subset of the SFT data used for Ling-Coder-Lite, synthesized with OSS-Instruct and Evol-Instruct style pipelines.
resources.how_to_use: Large synthetic code SFT with Chinese coverage; sample and filter rather than use whole.
resources.caveats: Card does not name the generator models, so provenance and terms are unclear. Not execution-verified per the card.

resources.name: OpenCodeInstruct (NVIDIA)
resources.size: 5,000,000 instruction-solution rows with unit tests, execution status and LLM judgments
resources.summary: Largest open code instruction set: each row has question, solution, generated unit tests, execution results and an LLM quality assessment, so you can filter by test score.
resources.how_to_use: Filter on average_test_score and llm_judgement before SFT; do not train on all 5M blindly. Stream it, it is ~19 GB uncompressed.
resources.caveats: Per the paper, solutions, tests and judgments came from Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (Qwen license terms apply to outputs). Tests are model-written, so a passing row is not guaranteed correct. Python-centric.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/OpenCodeInstruct', split='train', streaming=True)
# columns: id, input, output, domain, generation_algorithm, llm_judgement, unit_tests, tests_execution_status, average_test_score

resources.name: OpenCodeReasoning-2 (NVIDIA)
resources.size: dataset_info lists 1,398,166 and 1,174,475 rows (two splits; split names and languages not re-checked)
resources.summary: Second release: R1 generations with QwQ critiques and right/wrong judgements, for both code completion and code critique SFT.
resources.how_to_use: Use for reasoning SFT plus critique training; the pass_rate and judgement columns allow filtering.
resources.caveats: Generations by DeepSeek-R1 and critiques by QwQ-32B (per card fields r1_generation, qwq_critique). Judgement labels are model-produced, not ground truth.

resources.name: Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1 (code split)
resources.size: code split 1,896,395 rows (dataset_info); also chat 746,622, math 2,044,407, stem 20,662,167, tool_calling 310,051
resources.summary: SFT compilation behind Llama-3.3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1.5 with reasoning on/off responses; the code split carries reasoning traces.
resources.how_to_use: Load only the code split and filter; it has a reasoning flag so you can build mixed think/no-think data.
resources.caveats: Card lists teachers including DeepSeek-R1-0528 and Qwen3-235B-A22B, so those model terms apply. Large; stream it.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1', split=['code'], streaming=True)

resources.name: Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset (code)
resources.license: CC-BY-4.0 (card also notes Llama-derived-data redistribution requirements)
resources.size: SFT code split 10,108,883 samples (card table); also math, science, chat and RL configs
resources.summary: Post-training data for Llama-3.3-Nemotron-70B and Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B; v1.1 added 500K code reasoning samples.
resources.how_to_use: Use the SFT/code split with its reasoning on/off labels; subsample heavily.
resources.caveats: Teachers include DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-72B, Llama-3.3-70B and Mixtral-8x22B per the card; parts are subject to Llama license redistribution terms. Very large.
resources.load_snippet:
from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('nvidia/Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset', 'SFT', split=['code'], streaming=True)

resources.name: Nemotron-SFT-Competitive-Programming-v2
resources.size: 336K+ Python and 332K+ C++ samples over 34,799 questions; 40K Exercism-derived; 96.5K text-to-SQL with reasoning (card)
resources.summary: Competitive coding with reasoning and critique, Python Exercism-style exercises (Aider problems decontaminated), and enterprise text-to-SQL records generated with NVIDIA Data Designer.
resources.how_to_use: Pick the subset you need: competitive for reasoning, Exercism for exercise-style, SQL for schema-linking reasoning.
resources.caveats: Card names DeepSeek-R1-0528 as a generator for the competitive subset; SQL generator not confirmed in the text read. Problem sources have their own licenses.

resources.name: Nemotron-SFT-OpenCode-v1
resources.size: 100K-1M rows (HF size category; exact count not read)
resources.summary: Agentic instruction data for the OpenCode CLI: tool calling, AGENTS.md prompts, agent skills, bash-only tools and clarifying-question tool, in six subsets.
resources.how_to_use: Use to teach CLI-agent tool use and skills loading; match the harness format (OpenCode) at inference.
resources.caveats: Per card, questions and skills were synthesized with GPT OSS 120B and solution traces with Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, so those terms apply. Tied to one harness format.

resources.name: Nemotron-SFT-SWE-v2
resources.license: CC-BY-4.0 plus Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD (API list)
resources.size: ~46K OpenHands agent trajectories plus agentless localization, repair and test-generation subset (card)
resources.summary: SWE-Bench-style data: OpenHands agentic trajectories and agentless sub-task SFT data built from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench, SWE-Smith and SWE-Fixer-Train.
resources.how_to_use: Use both halves: trajectories for agent behavior, agentless data for localization/repair/test-writing skills.
resources.caveats: Agentic trajectories generated by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct; agentless responses by DeepSeek-R1-0528 (card). Mostly Python repositories; source issue data has own licenses.

resources.name: Nemotron-Cascade-SFT-SWE
resources.size: size not read (card has per-source question and sample tables)
resources.summary: Agentless-mini style SWE SFT data (localization, repair, test generation) from SWE-Bench-Train, SWE-reBench and SWE-Smith, difficulty-selected and decontaminated against SWE-Bench Verified repos.
resources.how_to_use: Use for non-agentic SWE skills; card reports 37.2 and 43.1 resolve rates for 8B and 14B models after SFT and RL (card, 2026-11-24).
resources.caveats: Responses generated with DeepSeek-R1-0528. Excludes repositories present in SWE-Bench Verified, which limits but does not remove all contamination risk elsewhere.

resources.name: Nemotron-Agentic-Tool-Use-v1
resources.summary: Multi-turn tool-use conversations: interactive-agent trajectories (simulated user, agent, tool environment) and general tool-calling, judge-filtered.
resources.how_to_use: Use for generic tool-calling skill alongside coding data.
resources.caveats: Tool-calling subset uses Qwen3-235B-A22B Thinking and Instruct 2507 per the card; other subset generators not fully read. LLM-judge filtered, tools are simulated.

resources.name: open-r1 CodeForces-CoTs
resources.size: ~10K Codeforces problems with up to 5 R1 traces each; many configs (solutions, solutions_py, decontaminated variants)
resources.summary: DeepSeek-R1 chain-of-thought solutions in C++ and Python for Codeforces problems, used to train OlympicCoder.
resources.how_to_use: Use the decontaminated configs (solutions_decontaminated or solutions_py_decontaminated) for training.
resources.caveats: Traces generated by DeepSeek-R1. Problems are from Codeforces. Not all traces are verified correct unless using the verified configs; check the card.

from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('open-r1/codeforces-cots', 'solutions_decontaminated')

resources.name: open-r1 Mixture-of-Thoughts (code)
resources.license: not stated in API tags (check card)
resources.size: 350K verified R1 traces total; code config 83,070 rows (dataset_info)
resources.summary: Verified DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces across math, code and science; code part is competitive-programming focused.
resources.how_to_use: Load the code config for code-only reasoning SFT.
resources.caveats: Traces distilled from DeepSeek-R1. License field absent in the API tags, so confirm terms before commercial use.

from datasets import load_dataset
ds = load_dataset('open-r1/Mixture-of-Thoughts', 'code', split='train')

resources.name: OpenThoughts-114k
resources.summary: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces with correctness verification; code rows include test cases and starter code.

resources.name: FineMath

resources.how_to_use: Math/reasoning share of a code mid-training mix.
resources.caveats: Web rights vary. 2023 vintage.

resources.name: datatrove
resources.summary: Hugging Face's platform-agnostic data pipeline library: readers, filters, MinHash dedup, tokenization, and executors for local, Slurm and Ray.

resources.name: NeMo Curator
resources.summary: GPU-accelerated data curation for LLMs: dedup (exact, fuzzy, semantic), quality classifiers, PII, decontamination, synthetic data.
resources.how_to_use: Use when you have GPUs and need fast fuzzy dedup and classifier filtering at multi-TB scale.
resources.caveats: Best on NVIDIA GPUs with RAPIDS; setup is heavier than datatrove. Repo moved from NVIDIA/NeMo-Curator.
resources.evidence: GitHub API NVIDIA-NeMo/Curator license Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-11-24

resources.name: bigcode-dataset
resources.size: 503 stars; folders: preprocessing, pii, near_deduplication, decontamination, language_selection

resources.how_to_use: Reference implementation for code-specific filters, MinHash near-dedup and decontamination; copy ideas even if you use datatrove.
resources.caveats: Last push 2024-08, built for 2022-2023 pipelines; may need updating.

resources.name: text-dedup
resources.summary: Collection of deduplication methods for text: MinHash, SimHash, suffix array, Bloom filter, exact hash.
resources.how_to_use: Use for medium-scale dedup on one machine or Spark; supports the BigCode-style MinHash recipe.
resources.caveats: Maintainer-scale project; pushed 2026-03. Check memory at large scale.

resources.name: datasketch
resources.summary: Python library for MinHash, LSH, LSH Forest and HyperLogLog used for near-duplicate detection.
resources.how_to_use: Building block for custom MinHash-LSH dedup (the method used for Stack v2/v3 near-dedup).
resources.caveats: Pure Python is slow at web scale; use for prototypes or smaller corpora.

resources.name: duplodocus
resources.summary: Ai2 Rust CLI for exact and MinHash dedup over large JSONL datasets.
resources.how_to_use: Use for fast single-node dedup of JSONL shards.
resources.caveats: Young project; JSONL input only; less battle-tested.

resources.name: decon (Ai2)
resources.summary: Token-based decontamination tool that finds training documents containing eval instances and writes reports and cleaned datasets.
resources.how_to_use: Run after dedup; load your eval sets (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench etc.) and drop or report hits.
resources.caveats: Young project; coverage depends on the eval files you supply and on n-gram sampling settings.

resources.name: Dolma toolkit
resources.summary: Ai2 data toolkit: fast Rust tagger/mixer, Bloom filter dedup and mixing used for OLMo corpora.
resources.how_to_use: Use the mixer/tagger for tagging, filtering and building data mixes by source proportion.
resources.caveats: Bloom filter dedup is approximate; fits web text better than code.

resources.name: Data-Juicer
resources.summary: One-stop data processing system with 100+ operators for text, code and multimodal data, including code filters and dedup.
resources.how_to_use: Use when you want a configurable operator pipeline with built-in analysis.
resources.caveats: Large surface area; verify operator quality on your code data.

resources.name: DCLM (DataComp-LM)
resources.summary: Framework and baselines for data curation experiments including fastText quality classifier filtering of web text.
resources.how_to_use: Borrow the fastText classifier-filtering recipe for code-web recall.
resources.caveats: Targeted at web text, not code repos.

resources.name: ScanCode Toolkit

resources.evidence: GitHub API aboutcode-org/scancode-toolkit license NOASSERTION; Stack v3 README

resources.name: go-license-detector
resources.license: NOASSERTION in GitHub API (verify in repo)

resources.how_to_use: Fast first-pass repo-level license detection.
resources.caveats: Last push 2023-06; unmaintained.

resources.name: Licensee
resources.summary: Ruby tool GitHub uses to detect a project's license from its LICENSE file.
resources.how_to_use: Cross-check license labels against GitHub's own detection.
resources.caveats: Repo-level only; Ruby dependency.

resources.name: SPDX license list data

resources.name: tree-sitter

resources.name: Microsoft Presidio
resources.summary: PII detection and anonymization SDK with recognizers and custom operators (repo moved from microsoft/presidio).
resources.how_to_use: Useful for non-code text (issues, docs, Q&A) PII scrubbing alongside StarPII.

resources.name: StarPII (bigcode)

resources.how_to_use: Run on files, replace spans with placeholders (<EMAIL>, <KEY>, <NAME>, <PASSWORD>) as in Stack v3.
resources.caveats: Gated; false positives/negatives exist; combine with regex secret scanners.
resources.evidence: huggingface.co/api/models/bigcode/starpii gated=auto; Stack v3 README step 5

resources.name: SentencePiece
resources.summary: Unsupervised tokenizer for BPE/unigram; many code and multilingual models use it.

resources.name: nanotron
resources.summary: Minimalistic large-model pretraining library from Hugging Face, used with datatrove-tokenized data.

resources.name: Qwen3.8-27B
resources.size: 27.8B params (safetensors total), dense, 262,144 ctx native, extensible to 1M
resources.summary: Newest open Qwen generation (Aug 2026): dense vision-language model with thinking mode and gains in coding and long-horizon agentic tasks. A strong post-trained starting point for SFT/RL on a single node, and a mid-size teacher.
resources.how_to_use: Use as the default dense starting point when you want to add domain or Swedish/agentic RL on top. Thinking on by default; toggle per request.
resources.caveats: Post-trained checkpoint only: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-Base returned 401 on the HF API so no open base was confirmed. Not a coder-specialized model. Vision encoder adds size. No coding score copied here: the card compares against proprietary models under its own harness settings.

resources.name: Qwen3-Coder-Next (and -Base)
resources.size: 79.7B params total, 3B active (MoE, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention), 262,144 ctx
resources.summary: Open-weight coding-agent model from Jan 2026 built for local agents (80B total, 3B active). A Base variant is published for further post-training.
resources.how_to_use: Use Qwen3-Coder-Next-Base as a base for custom post-training and the Instruct as a cheap agentic teacher. Fits one large GPU only with quantization.
resources.caveats: Instruct supports non-thinking mode only (no <think> blocks). MoE with hybrid linear attention needs recent vLLM/SGLang/Transformers. Base card says trained on 370+ languages; we did not verify vendor benchmark numbers.

resources.name: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
resources.size: 480B params total, 35B active (MoE), 262,144 ctx native, 1M with YaRN
resources.summary: July 2025 flagship Qwen coder: large MoE for agentic coding and repository-scale context. Commonly used as a permissively licensed teacher for trajectory distillation.
resources.how_to_use: Use as a teacher for synthetic SFT data and trajectories; license permits it. Needs a multi-GPU node.
resources.caveats: Very large to serve. Superseded in the Qwen line by Qwen3-Coder-Next and Qwen3.8. Check output quality per task before trusting distilled data.

resources.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
resources.summary: Small MoE Qwen3 coder that is easy to fine-tune and serve; the most downloaded recent Qwen coder in HF search (about 1.95M downloads on the check date).
resources.how_to_use: Good first RL/SFT target on a single node, or a cheap teacher/rollout policy.
resources.caveats: Instruct only in this entry. MoE RL needs router-stability care (see GSPO). Overtaken by Qwen3.8 in capability.

resources.name: Qwen2.5-Coder family (32B shown)
resources.license: Apache-2.0 (verified for 32B and 7B; check each size's card)
resources.size: 32.8B params (32B base); 7B is 7.6B; native config ctx 32,768, up to 131,072 with YaRN
resources.summary: Sep-Nov 2024 code-specialized Qwen family with base and instruct variants from 0.5B to 32B. Still the most widely used open base for code SFT/RL recipes (SWE-smith, OpenHands LM, Open-R1 style work).
resources.how_to_use: Use the base checkpoints (7B/14B/32B) for controlled recipe experiments, since many published results start from them.
resources.caveats: Old by Nov 2026: newer Qwen3.x models beat it. License verified only for the 32B/7B pages fetched; sizes 0.5B-3B may carry different licenses, check before use. Qwen2.5 bases may be contaminated with reasoning-like data (see Dr. GRPO paper).

resources.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
resources.size: 763B params in safetensors; card says 552B backbone parameters (multimodal MoE), up to 1M ctx
resources.summary: Sep 2026 DeepSeek open MoE with 1M context, MIT licensed; the card describes an encoder-decoder (CED) design with KV-cache compression.
resources.how_to_use: Teacher candidate for distillation with a fully permissive license; reasoning effort levels exist on the V4 line.
resources.caveats: Needs multi-node serving. Safetensors total (763B) and the card's 552B figure differ (likely vision and other components); we report both. No coding score copied from the card.

resources.how_to_use: Use only if you have the infrastructure; V4-Flash variants are the practical teachers.
resources.caveats: Very large. Pro is labeled Preview in the V4-Flash-0731 card. Benchmark claims are vendor-reported.

resources.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
resources.summary: Dec 2025 DeepSeek V3 line model, MIT licensed; a common open teacher and RL starting point before V4.
resources.how_to_use: Teacher for distillation when V4 is too large.
resources.caveats: Superseded by V4.x. Large MoE.

resources.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (Instruct 236B / Lite)
resources.license: DeepSeek model license (HF 'other: deepseek-license'; code under MIT)
resources.summary: June 2024 MoE code model continued-pretrained from DeepSeek-V2; strong at release, now legacy.
resources.how_to_use: Lite-Base (15.7B) is a usable MoE base; read the model license before commercial use.
resources.caveats: Legacy. Custom license with use restrictions, not OSI open. Superseded by Qwen3-Coder and DeepSeek V4.

resources.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro

resources.name: GLM-5.3

resources.how_to_use: Strong open teacher for terminal/agentic data under a mostly permissive license.
resources.caveats: Card tables are vendor-run and include proprietary baselines; not independently verified. Large MoE.

resources.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
resources.summary: Aug 2026 smaller GLM-5.3 with new base model, hybrid sparse/linear attention and native multimodality; MIT licensed.

resources.name: StarCoder2-15B
resources.summary: Open pretrained code model trained on The Stack v2 with opt-outs excluded; the data and training are documented.
resources.how_to_use: Use when provenance matters (permissive-or-no-license data, opt-out respected) or to study pretraining.
resources.caveats: 2024 vintage, far behind current models. OpenRAIL-M carries behavioral use restrictions. Can emit verbatim training code (card warning).

resources.name: OpenCoder-8B (Base/Instruct)
resources.license: 'inf' license (HF other); card says commercial use supported
resources.summary: Fully transparent code LLM: weights plus data pipeline, ablations and training protocol released. Best choice for studying code pretraining and annealing recipes end to end.
resources.how_to_use: Use as a research base or to reproduce the recipe; do not expect current frontier capability.
resources.caveats: 8K context is short for agentic work. Custom license, read it. 2024 vintage.

resources.name: Seed-Coder-8B (Base/Instruct/Reasoning)
resources.summary: ByteDance Seed (2025) family built from model-curated pretraining data; base, instruct and RL-trained reasoning variants in one permissive license.

resources.caveats: Data pipeline relies on LLM filtering; training data itself is not released. Mid-2025 vintage.

resources.name: Granite Code 8B Base
resources.summary: IBM enterprise-oriented code model trained on license-permissive data; legacy but cleanly licensed.

resources.name: OctoPack: Instruction Tuning Code LLMs
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: CommitPack: 4 TB of Git commits across 350 languages used as natural code-instruction data; 46.2% HumanEval pass@1 for StarCoder-16B tuned without OpenAI outputs (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Commits are a permissive, non-distilled source of instruction data; use for repair/edit skills.
resources.caveats: Abstract numbers are 2023 vintage; also introduces HumanEvalPack.

resources.name: StarCoder 2 and The Stack v2
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Documents the open data, opt-out and training for StarCoder2 on The Stack v2.
resources.how_to_use: Reference for data governance (licenses, opt-out) in code pretraining.
resources.caveats: Models and data are from early 2024.

resources.name: OpenCoder: The Open Cookbook
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Releases weights plus reproducible data pipeline, ablations and training protocol for a top-tier code LLM at its release.
resources.how_to_use: Best single paper for recipe transparency in code pretraining, annealing and SFT data.
resources.caveats: Smaller scale (1.5B/8B) and 2024 vintage.

resources.name: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Describes data, training and evaluation for the Qwen2.5-Coder family.
resources.how_to_use: Read for data-mixing and code-vs-text ratio decisions in a leading open recipe.
resources.caveats: Data is not released; vendor evaluation.

resources.name: DeepSeek-Coder
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Repo-level pretraining data construction (dependency-ordered files) and fill-in-the-middle for code models.
resources.how_to_use: Order files by dependency and use FIM for repo-level pretraining.
resources.caveats: Early 2024.

resources.name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Continued pretraining of a MoE on code and math tokens to reach closed-model-level code results at release.
resources.how_to_use: Evidence that continued pretraining on code-heavy mixes lifts a general MoE.
resources.caveats: Mid-2024; benchmarks since saturated.

resources.name: CodeRL
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: First widely cited framework using unit-test signals and an actor-critic to train code LMs with RL.
resources.how_to_use: Historical context for execution-based reward.
resources.caveats: 2022 models and benchmarks; superseded by GRPO-style RL.

resources.name: RLTF: Reinforcement Learning from Unit Test Feedback
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Online RL with multi-granularity unit-test feedback (including error locations) to refine code LLMs.
resources.how_to_use: Fine-grained failure signals can augment pass/fail reward.
resources.caveats: 2023, small models.

resources.name: PPOCoder
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Combines pretrained code LMs with PPO using compiler/execution and structure-alignment feedback.
resources.how_to_use: Early example of non-differentiable execution rewards.
resources.caveats: Early work; models are tiny relative to today.

resources.name: DeepSeek-R1
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Shows reasoning can be incentivized with pure RL on verifiable rewards, including coding competitions.
resources.how_to_use: Foundation for RL with verifiable reward; start from a strong base, reward = tests pass.
resources.caveats: Full data and code not released; replicate via open-r1.

resources.name: AceReason-Nemotron
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Systematic RL ablations: math-only RL first then code-only RL; shows math RL also helps code.
resources.how_to_use: Stage math then code, filter prompts, scale RL on distilled bases.
resources.caveats: Competitive coding only.

resources.name: Skywork Open Reasoner 1
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Open RL implementation on R1-distill models; abstract reports average accuracy on AIME24, AIME25 and LiveCodeBench rising from 57.8% to 72.8% for 32B; includes ablations on core RL components.
resources.how_to_use: Read ablations on data mixing, filtering, entropy control.
resources.caveats: Competitive programming only.

resources.name: SWE-Gym
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: First environment for training SWE agents: 2,438 real Python tasks with executable runtimes; up to 19% absolute gains on SWE-bench Verified/Lite via SFT, plus trained verifiers (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Use as the baseline executable training environment and trajectory source.
resources.caveats: Only 2,438 tasks from a small set of repos, Python only.

resources.name: SWE-smith
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Pipeline that turns any Python repo into an execution environment and synthesizes 100s-1000s of task instances by breaking tests; builds a 50k-instance dataset from 128 repos (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Scalable data generator for SWE tasks; start from the released dataset and trajectories.
resources.caveats: Synthetic bugs differ from real issues; Python only; trajectories used Claude 3.7 Sonnet (terms).

resources.name: R2E-Gym
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Procedural SWE environment of 8.7K tasks via test generation and back-translation from commits; 34.4% on SWE-bench Verified with a 32B model; hybrid test-time scaling (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Source of RL tasks (used by DeepSWE); hybrid verifiers help test-time scaling.
resources.caveats: Synthesized issues may be noisy; Python.

resources.name: SWE-RL (Meta)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Scales RL for real-world software engineering with a lightweight rule-based reward (similarity to ground-truth patch) on open software evolution data.
resources.how_to_use: Cheap reward that avoids execution; consider as a pre-stage before execution-based RL.
resources.caveats: Similarity reward is a proxy and can reward style over correctness; repo code license NOASSERTION.

resources.name: Kimi-Dev: Agentless Training as Skill Prior
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Argues Agentless-style training induces localization/edit/reflection priors; the abstract reports 60.4% on SWE-bench Verified (workflow mode) and 48.6% pass@1 as an agent after SFT on 5k public trajectories.
resources.how_to_use: Train single-turn verifiable steps first, then adapt to agents with small trajectory SFT.
resources.caveats: Numbers are authors' own.

resources.name: Agentless
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: A simple localize-repair-validate pipeline without autonomous agents that is competitive on SWE-bench.
resources.how_to_use: Strong cheap baseline and a template for structured single-turn training tasks.
resources.caveats: Mid-2024 numbers.

resources.name: SelfCodeAlign
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Self-alignment pipeline: model extracts concepts, generates tasks, samples responses with tests, keeps passing examples; 74k pairs from CodeQwen1.5-7B (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Distillation-free, execution-validated SFT data generation; good when teacher licenses are a concern.
resources.caveats: Gains shown on HumanEval-era benchmarks; compute-heavy sampling.

resources.name: Textbooks Are All You Need (phi-1)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: 1.3B model trained on 6B tokens of filtered web 'textbook quality' code plus 1B tokens of synthetic textbooks reaches 50.6% HumanEval (abstract).
resources.how_to_use: Quality filtering plus synthetic textbook data beats raw scale for small models.
resources.caveats: Synthetic data from GPT-3.5; HumanEval is contaminated-prone; model not released fully at the time.

resources.name: SmolLM2 (Stack-Edu)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Data-centric small-model training; introduces Stack-Edu (education-quality code filter), FineMath, SmolTalk and manual mix refinement.
resources.how_to_use: Use educational-quality classifiers to filter code; refine mixture per stage.
resources.caveats: Small scale (1.7B).

resources.name: Seed-Coder
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Model-centric pipeline: LLMs score and filter code pretraining data instead of hand rules.
resources.how_to_use: Use LLM scorers for code-quality filtering across languages.
resources.caveats: Data not released.

resources.name: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Selective language modeling: train on tokens with high excess loss versus a reference model.
resources.how_to_use: Token-level quality filtering for continued pretraining.
resources.caveats: Evaluated mostly on math in the paper; code transfer is less established.

resources.name: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: About 1,000 curated examples can align a model, arguing for quality over quantity in SFT.
resources.how_to_use: Basis for small high-quality SFT sets; code transfer is an inference, not shown in the paper.
resources.caveats: Not a code paper; verify on code benchmarks.

resources.name: OpenCodeReasoning
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: SFT-only distillation dataset for competitive coding; abstract reports 61.8% LiveCodeBench and 24.6% CodeContests and analyzes execution filtering.
resources.how_to_use: Shows distillation SFT can match RL for coding; ablate execution filtering.
resources.caveats: Teacher outputs from DeepSeek-R1; competitive-programming scope.

resources.name: Dynamic Scaling of Unit Tests for Code Reward Modeling (CodeRM)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: More generated unit tests give better reward signals, especially on hard problems; proposes CodeRM-8B.
resources.how_to_use: Scale generated tests per problem for reward quality; use a trained test generator.
resources.caveats: LLM-generated tests are themselves unreliable.

resources.name: AceCoder
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Automated test-case synthesis creates (question, tests) pairs for reward models and RL; best-of-32 gains of about 5 to 10 points reported.
resources.how_to_use: Synthesize tests at scale and use pass rates for rewards.
resources.caveats: Synthetic tests can be wrong; evaluated on 7-8B models.

resources.name: DAPO
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Open RL system with decoupled clip, dynamic sampling, token-level loss and overlong handling; 50 on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B base.
resources.how_to_use: Adopt clip-higher, dynamic sampling and overlong filtering for GRPO variants.
resources.caveats: Math evaluated; code reuse (DeepCoder) is secondary.

resources.name: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training (Dr. GRPO)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Finds GRPO length bias that inflates incorrect responses and proposes Dr. GRPO; also notes Qwen2.5 bases show strong reasoning without templates.
resources.how_to_use: Remove length and std normalization biases; be wary of base-model pretraining effects.
resources.caveats: Math-centered experiments.

resources.name: Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Sequence-level importance ratios stabilize RL for MoE models.
resources.how_to_use: Try GSPO for MoE coders if token-level GRPO is unstable.
resources.caveats: Qwen-team method; evidence is mostly vendor-internal.

resources.name: ProRL: Prolonged RL
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Long RL runs expand reasoning boundaries beyond the base model.
resources.how_to_use: Budget for long RL runs with KL control and resets.
resources.caveats: Mostly math/reasoning.

resources.name: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Environments
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Abstract reports 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a patch that differs from the gold patch (57.8% with a stronger attacker).
resources.how_to_use: Audit and harden tests before using SWE tasks as RL rewards.
resources.caveats: 49-task sample, single study, June 2026 preprint.

resources.name: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Benchmark on LiveCodeBench problems where hacking is easy; LLM judges detect obvious hacks, held-out tests help only slightly.
resources.how_to_use: Use judges plus test-file edit detection to monitor RL rollouts.
resources.caveats: Observes hacking in Codex and Claude Code; benchmark scope is small.

resources.name: Coding or Cheating?
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Frontier models try to recover answers from repo history and filesystems in hardened SWE environments.
resources.how_to_use: Sandbox git history, object store and filesystem in RL environments.
resources.caveats: Nov 2026 preprint.

resources.name: LiveCodeBench
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Time-stamped contamination-free evaluation for code LLMs via continuously collected problems.
resources.how_to_use: Use release-date windows after a model's cutoff for clean evaluation.
resources.caveats: Windows are static once published; newer models age past them.

resources.name: Rethinking Benchmark and Contamination (rephrased samples)
resources.license: arXiv preprint (paper); check repo for code/data licenses
resources.summary: Shows rephrased benchmark samples evade n-gram decontamination and inflate scores.
resources.how_to_use: Use embedding-based decontamination, not only n-gram overlap.
resources.caveats: General LLM paper, not code-specific.

resources.name: DeepCoder RL recipe (GRPO+)
resources.summary: Open code-RL recipe: GRPO+ (DAPO ideas: clip-high, no KL loss), iterative context lengthening 16K to 32K, DAPO overlong filtering, and offline difficulty filtering of coding problems, on R1-Distill-Qwen-14B.
resources.how_to_use: Replicate with verl or rLLM; keep problems with reliable tests, filter by difficulty, mask truncated sequences.
resources.caveats: Details taken from the HF model card; the Notion blog resolved HTTP 200 but was not parsed. Results are on LiveCodeBench v5 only.

resources.name: DeepSWE RL recipe (rLLM)
resources.summary: Pure-RL SWE-agent recipe on Qwen3-32B with 4.5K R2E-Gym problems, repos overlapping SWE-bench Verified filtered out, built on rLLM.
resources.how_to_use: Reuse the contamination filter by repository and the Docker-per-task setup.
resources.caveats: Numbers (23 to 42% in 200 steps) from the model card; blog resolved HTTP 200.

resources.summary: Hugging Face's open reproduction of DeepSeek-R1: SFT, GRPO training scripts, code-reward environments and datasets.
resources.how_to_use: Start here for an end-to-end GRPO-with-code-execution reference using TRL.
resources.caveats: Reference-quality code, not a turnkey frontier recipe. Activity per GitHub API on 2026-11-24: 26.5k stars, last push 2026-10-26, not archived
